challenge: Let a shopper judge fabric, colour and build quality before paying, from evidence rather than the seller's photos.

title: Labels that hide the sugar and the milk
problem: Health-conscious shoppers cannot easily tell how much sugar a packaged snack holds, because the labels are hard to read. Parents struggle to spot the ultra-processed, high-sugar snacks that dominate quick-commerce listings, and in December 2025 most said they wanted clear red warnings on the front of the pack. Parents of a baby with a milk-protein allergy struggle to find safe substitutes, in the shop and in the kitchen.
challenge: Let a parent know in one glance whether a packaged food is right for their child.

title: Chasing suppliers by phone, one invoice at a time
problem: In a June 2026 LocalCircles survey, about 2 in 3 MSMEs said they struggle to manage multiple suppliers, and half reported constant follow-ups and invoices that fail GST checks, blocking their input credit. Complex supply chains still run on spreadsheets and phone calls, so disruptions beyond the direct supplier go unseen.
challenge: Take supplier follow-ups and invoice fixes off a small owner's phone, so no input credit is lost to a bad bill.

title: The same strip of tablets costs half next door
problem: The same prescription can cost 30 to 50 percent more at one pharmacy than another, and patients cannot compare. Online orders are approved and then cancelled days later because the partner shop never had the stock, leaving patients without medicine.
challenge: Tell a patient where their prescription is in stock today, nearby, and at the lowest price.

title: Holding the licence and losing the dispute anyway
problem: Creators who paid for a stock music licence, or used only the official licensed audio library, still get Content ID claims, unlisted videos and rejected disputes. In October 2026 one claim hit a Short with hundreds of thousands of views, and the music could not be swapped without reposting and losing them. Digital sellers with a clear no-refund policy lose buyer disputes the same way.
challenge: Make a creator's proof of rights impossible to ignore, attached and ready the moment a claim lands.

title: Evenings lost to chasing invoices by hand
problem: Micro businesses spend 10 or more hours a week making, chasing and matching invoices by hand, because ERP software is too heavy for them. Late-paying customers strain small suppliers, and contractors lose their evenings chasing what they are owed instead of doing billable work or being with family.
challenge: Get a small owner paid on time without a single evening spent chasing.

title: Paying in full before anyone checks the work
problem: Deep cleaning varies wildly, with missed areas and no checklist or way to verify the work, and in September 2026 a harsh acid ruined a bathroom's chrome fittings and left the taps leaking, with no remedy offered. Carpentry has to be paid for in full before the quality can be checked, and defects show up after installation. The household carries the risk of work it cannot inspect.
challenge: Let a household sign off a cleaning or carpentry job from before-and-after photos before the final payment.

title: A course business the host can cut overnight
problem: Course creators build years of income on teaching marketplaces and hosts that can change terms at will: one forced shift to subscription payouts cut earnings by over ninety percent, and another educator was terminated without notice. Long-time sellers leave over rising prices and weak support, and tutors want more control over their business than the software allows. The audience and income belong to the host, not the teacher.
challenge: Let a course creator move their students, content and payments to a home they own in one weekend.

title: On ONDC, then no orders once the discounts stop
problem: About 85% of shops onboarded to ONDC never transact meaningfully, and retail orders fell about 35% from their peak once buyer discounts ended. Sellers juggle separate services for discovery, fulfilment, delivery and payment, and inconsistent logistics partners turn the few orders they do get into failures.
challenge: Get a small shop its first 10 repeat online orders without paying for discounts.

title: Automations that break more than the work they replace
problem: Workflow automation breaks often or takes more setup than the task itself, so people keep repeating the same tedious steps every day, and say they would pay for something dependable. Many workflows still need a person clicking through websites and desktop programs that offer no other way in, and one small marketing agency hand-builds scripts for client work because nothing off the shelf fits.
challenge: Let an office worker hand over one daily chore by showing it once, and have it still work next month.

title: Clothes that stop fitting after a handful of washes
problem: Mass-market garments lose their shape within a handful of washes, and cotton-spandex blends shrink badly even when washed cold and hung to dry, so a correctly sized purchase stops fitting within weeks. Silk sarees and embroidered outfits fare worse, ruined by local dry cleaners who use harsh chemicals. The result is paying again and again to replace clothes.
challenge: Tell a shopper how a garment will survive washing, and how to wash it, before it is ruined.

title: Home bakers pricing by gut, selling at a loss
problem: Home bakers and small-batch cooks find a full online store overkill, so they take orders over chat and price by gut feel without tracking what the ingredients cost, and many sell at a loss without knowing it. Tiffin services serve the same fixed menu every day, with no way to swap a dish for an allergy, a diet or taste.
challenge: Let a home cook take an order, price every dish at a profit and handle swaps, all from a phone.

title: Load boards full of stale and phantom freight
problem: Owner-operators pay rising subscriptions for load boards that show stale posts, the same load reposted by competing brokers, and fewer listings after unexplained algorithm changes. New carriers cannot get booked for months and brokers are shifting to fixed trusted partners, leaving one-truck operators without steady freight.
challenge: Help a one-truck carrier find real, bookable loads without paying for noise.

title: Fitness plans easy to buy, impossible to cancel
problem: Diet and fitness programmes are sold through limited-time offers and sales promises, then refuse refunds, hide deadlines in the terms and keep billing after cancellation. Members and even trainers report being charged months after they tried to leave.
challenge: Make cancelling a fitness or diet subscription take one minute and leave a record the seller cannot dispute.

title: The counter-notice that hands your details to the harasser
problem: Impostors file false copyright strikes against small channels, and fighting back means a counter-notice that sends the creator's personal details straight to the person attacking them. In October 2026 a gaming creator took 3 strikes in a day from someone posing as a game publisher on a free email address, enough to put the channel at risk of deletion. Reports of real stalking, meanwhile, go unmoderated.
challenge: Help a creator beat a false strike within a day without giving the attacker their personal details.

title: The chargeback you had proof for, and still lost
problem: Small online merchants lose chargeback disputes they could have won, because writing an evidence-backed response is slow and confusing and the payment provider rarely helps. In September 2026 one merchant holding documentary evidence on a large dispute could not get any response from the gateway's support team. Bots testing stolen cards add more disputes, and funds stay held while every order is checked by hand.
challenge: Turn a merchant's order and delivery records into a chargeback reply that wins, in minutes rather than an evening.

title: Paid rental search: 1 viewing in 20 days
problem: Renters pay for premium search plans promising dozens of matching homes and a set number of owner contacts, then get 1 viewing in 20 days, or none. A Housing.com buyer got a few suggestions across a whole 45-day plan, and one relationship manager admitted having no verified properties at all. Ask for a refund and the answer is that the service was already used.
challenge: Get a renter 5 real viewings that match their brief within a week.

title: 6 months of job-portal premium, a handful of calls
problem: Indian job seekers pay for premium job-portal plans that promise recruiter visibility, then get fewer calls than they did applying by hand. One subscriber got a handful of recruiter calls across 6 months, and an experienced professional with an accurate, updated profile says the portal only works for freshers. What arrives instead is a stream of repeated or irrelevant listings.
challenge: Show a job seeker, before they pay, how many real recruiter calls a profile like theirs gets.

title: Re-entering the whole catalogue every time the till dies
problem: Small shops keep switching point-of-sale vendors as subsidised terminals break, startups fold or prices climb, and every switch means re-entering the catalogue and retraining staff. One store's card terminal stopped working, so staff keyed card numbers by hand while the subscription went up by $40 a month. A growing shop that outgrew its till went through 3 systems, paying for each migration.
challenge: Move a shop from one billing system to another in an hour, with catalogue, prices and history intact.

title: Firms bought AI and still do the work themselves
problem: Firms that buy AI still do the legal and professional work themselves, because what they bought helps a person do the job rather than handing back the finished result. Cleaning messy data and combining many documents into one reliable decision stayed a repetitive manual chore in reports from February 2025 to May 2026, across many industries.
challenge: Hand a firm one finished piece of back-office work, like a cleaned dataset or a decision memo, not another assistant.

title: Return pickups that never come
problem: Online fashion returns stall at the doorstep: pickups are rescheduled for weeks with false notes that the customer was unavailable, or happen only during working hours when buyers are out. Even after a pickup, refunds sit pending for weeks with no status or escalation route, and some arrive only after a formal consumer complaint.
challenge: Get a stuck return picked up and refunded within a week, without the buyer spending an hour on support.

title: The tiffin business that breaks at 50 customers
problem: Home tiffin cooks running subscriptions on notebooks and WhatsApp lose track of payments, pauses and dues once they pass about 40–50 customers. Cottage-food rules keep home bakers to a residential oven, so output stays capped and per-unit costs stay high as demand grows. The next step, a rented commercial kitchen, means paying recurring rent before the revenue exists to cover it.
challenge: Give a home food business a cheap, safe step between the home kitchen and a rented one.

title: Hauled the load, then the broker vanished
problem: Owner-operators haul loads that were secretly re-brokered, then go unpaid when the middleman disappears. Wrong charges take months to resolve and unexplained account holds freeze earnings for a week, so one dispute can cost the loads a small carrier needs to stay afloat.
challenge: Make sure a small carrier knows who is really paying before the truck is loaded.

title: Small gyms lose money between card and payout
problem: Small gyms pay monthly software fees plus card charges, then wait on erratic payouts of their own members' fees. Billing systems lock loyal members out the instant a payment fails and double-charge others, while coaches still have to be paid by hand outside the system.
challenge: Show a small gym owner every rupee a member paid, when it lands, and who is owed what, in one view.

title: A finished edit, locked in by an expired trial
problem: Freelance video editors working from phones find that free editors lack the blending modes, colour grading and transitions paid client work needs. Pay for a trial instead and it can end early: in September 2026 one creator was refused even temporary access to export a project they had already finished. Generative video became affordable in 2025, and an editor who adopts it early can win work that used to need a studio.
challenge: Help a freelance editor deliver client-grade video from a phone, with the export always in their own hands.

title: Money debited, transaction failed, nobody owns the refund
problem: Payments get debited while the merchant, gateway or booking site shows them as failed, and the refund goes missing as each side points at the other. It happens to train tickets, pension contributions and gateway checkouts alike, and the money can sit for days with no owner and no status. Salaried taxpayers waited months for refunds with no visible reason, risking the deadline to revise their returns.
challenge: Get a stuck refund back to the payer without them chasing both companies.

title: A short walk to the metro, says the ad
problem: Property ads promise a short walk to the metro when the real peak-hour commute is far longer, and portals stay full of ghost listings for homes already sold or rented. In September 2026 a developer found unverified listings of its own project on Housing.com with no way to control them. Buyers making huge purchases still lack reliable data on schools, safety, air, water and power cuts.
challenge: Tell a home seeker the real commute, power cuts and air quality for any address in under a minute.

title: Paid for a resume writer, got a template
problem: Job seekers in India pay for resume writing, job-lead add-ons and personal job experts, and get generic content, emailed feeds of public listings, or a relationship manager who vanishes after payment. Features that once helped freshers for free now sit behind paid tiers that do not deliver, a complaint that kept coming up from October 2025 to September 2026. Candidates lose money at the point they can least afford it.
challenge: Give a fresher the resume and job-lead help they were sold, at a fraction of the price, and prove it worked.

title: A personal assistant, but only if you're rich
problem: Help with errands, admin and planning has only ever been affordable for the wealthy. Meeting the right people is no easier: matching by shared interest for activities, services or dating is still unsolved, and single people in their 40s say they would pay well for real help getting past first dates. Voice and agent models became good enough in 2025 to make calls, fill forms and book things for someone.
challenge: Give an ordinary person the errands, admin and introductions help that used to need a personal assistant.

title: Salons paying commission on their own regulars
problem: Booking software sold to small salons and solo stylists charges marketplace commission on clients who were already theirs, adds per-message and per-card fees, and changes plans without warning. The monthly bill becomes impossible to predict, and some owners give up and go back to a paper diary.
challenge: Let a solo stylist take bookings and deposits from their own clients without paying a cut on every visit.

title: The free days the milk subscription never gave
problem: Milk and food subscribers find benefits withdrawn after signing up, offers only partly honoured, deliveries erratic and items silently out of stock. In January 2026 a dairy subscriber got only part of a promised free-days offer and was refused help without screenshots, and another paid for an address later declared unserviceable. Paid food-delivery members lost their rain-surge exemption in 2025 and now pay the surcharge anyway.
challenge: Show a subscriber what was promised against what arrived, and get the difference back in one message.

title: Small sellers pay the steepest courier rates going
problem: Online sellers spend up to an hour a day comparing courier prices across zones and weight slabs, and still pay full rates that large shippers never see. Returns and replacements cost even more to ship than forward orders, and discounted aggregator rates can end up above going direct.
challenge: Cut what a small seller pays per parcel without adding an hour of rate-checking to their day.

title: 6 months for a fix, and no way out
problem: Small studios and solo therapists wait months for fixes, get pushed through AI bots before any human help, and absorb new fees added without notice. One wellness practitioner waited 6 months for a scheduling fix, and a solo therapist was hit with a new per-claim fee while long-used features were removed. Leaving feels impossible, because every client, package and booking lives inside the vendor's records.
challenge: Let a small practice move every client, package and booking to a new provider in one afternoon.

title: Translation is either 8 hours or wrong
problem: Creators and small publishers working in less common languages get auto-captions they cannot remove and machine translations that still need checking line by line. Agencies are overkill for small jobs, so one website owner spent 8 or more hours per file translating by hand. In September 2026 a creator in a niche language still could not remove wrong captions, even after uploading correct subtitles.
challenge: Get a small publisher's video or page into another language, checked and accurate, in under an hour.

title: Locked out after a death or a lost phone
problem: After a death, families spend months reaching scattered accounts, documents and assets because succession paperwork is slow and few people prepare. Losing an email account or a phone holding authentication codes can lock someone out of banking and work with no human to help.
challenge: Make sure the people who need your accounts can reach them, and nobody else can.

title: The co-living room that changes after you pay
problem: Co-living and PG residents face undisclosed upfront fees, unreliable internet, unauthorised rent increases and eviction threats. Bookings are confirmed without real availability, residents get moved to worse rooms, and in April 2026 one managed-rental tenant was charged move-out fees for damage the manager's own staff had caused. Co-living has grown fast in Indian cities since 2024, and complaints about hidden fees grew with it.
challenge: Let a tenant compare co-living operators on what residents actually paid and got, before they sign.

title: Hiring an accountant, getting a mechanic
problem: Small Indian employers pay for job posts and get a trickle of mismatched, duplicate or inactive applicants, with slow support when they complain. In July 2026 one business paid about ₹3,000 for a post and got 11 applicants, including a mechanic for an accountant role; another ran a 3-month hiring plan and made no hires at all. A premium portal can do worse than a cheaper one.
challenge: Get a small business 3 qualified candidates for a role within a week, without another paid post.

title: Freelance income decided by a ranking nobody explains
problem: Established freelancers with perfect feedback watch client invitations collapse overnight when a marketplace changes its ranking, with no explanation and no way to recover. Fees keep rising, a single unfair rating on a refunded order cannot be contested, and generated proposals now bury real ones, so years of reputation can stop paying without warning.
challenge: Give a freelancer a steady flow of clients that no single marketplace's ranking change can switch off.

title: The ice cream that melted, and nobody's fault
problem: Frozen food and ice cream ordered online often arrive melted and refrozen, and paneer arrives sour, with no way for the buyer to tell where the cold chain broke. In August 2026 one buyer's ice cream came melted and support offered an unrelated coupon instead of a refund; days later another was told sour paneer was the brand's problem. Nobody pays for a broken cold chain, so it keeps breaking.
challenge: Make a broken cold chain visible to the buyer and costly to whoever broke it.

title: Delivery attempted, says the courier who never called
problem: Last-mile agents log failed delivery attempts without calling or visiting, so parcels bounce back and orders get cancelled while the buyer sat at home. Xpressbees agents log a single missed ring as a failed attempt, and buyers reported the same story again and again between September 2025 and September 2026. Each time they reorder, wait for a refund and chase support that cannot help.
challenge: Make a false delivery attempt cost the courier, not the buyer waiting at home.

title: Matching aggregator visits to bookings by hand
problem: Corporate fitness aggregators grew fast in 2025, and studios and clinics now run bookings, aggregator visits, invoices and accounting in separate places that barely connect, matching visits and recurring packages by hand. Some practice software cannot even issue recurring invoices or membership packages. Across healthcare, roughly a third of spending goes on administration created by disconnected systems and paperwork.
challenge: Turn a month of bookings, aggregator visits and invoices into one reconciled ledger without a spreadsheet.

title: The fake manager quoting double in a creator's name
problem: Over half of Indian creators surveyed in May 2025 had lost brand deals because brands had no verified way to reach them directly. Fake talent managers fill the gap, impersonating creators and quoting double their rates, so brands walk away from deals the creator never knew existed. One founder who contacted 600 creators found the deal admin pain real, but not yet painful enough to pay for.
challenge: Make sure a brand that wants a creator reaches the creator, not someone pretending to manage them.

title: Input credit lost because a supplier filed late
problem: Small businesses lose input tax credit whenever a supplier files late or invoices fail to appear in their auto-drafted returns, and stricter matching now triggers notices for small mismatches. Reconciling books against returns at year end is slow, and errors surface only when the notice arrives.
challenge: Catch every GST mismatch in the month it happens, not when the notice lands.

title: Housing societies find tank cleaners by word of mouth
problem: Apartment societies struggle to find and schedule water tank cleaning, wait months for municipal pruning of dangerous branches before the monsoon, and find no quick private service to assess risky trees. Where management firms are hired, boards say they hide behind a portal and lose contact with residents. Upkeep slips until something breaks or falls.
challenge: Let a housing society book, track and verify every seasonal upkeep job from one shared calendar.

title: Hours of lectures and podcasts, almost nothing retained
problem: Learners take in hours of podcasts, books, articles and recorded lectures and forget most of it within days, despite highlighting and notes. Notes end up long and messy, backlogs of recorded classes pile up across subjects, and nothing brings back what was learned when it is needed. Time spent learning turns into very little knowledge kept.
challenge: Make what someone heard or read this week come back to them at the moment it is useful.

title: Locked out of your earnings with nobody to call
problem: Freelancers and tiny consultancies can lose access overnight to the account that holds their clients, bids and invoices, through a vague suspension, a restriction mid-bidding or a login failure. In October 2026 one freelancer was restricted mid-bid after paying for connects and visibility boosts, and could not reach a single human. Deadlines slip and a whole income channel goes dark while they wait.
challenge: Make sure a freelancer locked out of any one account still has their clients, invoices and history the same day.

title: Dinner decided at the last minute, again
problem: Hosts planning a last-minute get-together cannot put good food together quickly, because shopping and cooking take hours. Office workers grab fried snacks in the late afternoon because nothing healthy is nearby, and tracking what is already in the kitchen is so tedious to set up that most people give up. So every food decision gets made late, and badly.
challenge: Make tonight's food plan in 2 minutes, using what is already in the kitchen.

title: Return to origin bills the seller twice for nothing
problem: Parcels come back to small sellers marked return to origin after attempts that never happened, so the seller pays shipping both ways and loses the sale. Wrong or damaged returns arrive, claims are denied without a clear evidence process, and lost return parcels stay unrefunded for weeks.
challenge: Cut a small seller's return-to-origin losses by half within a month.

title: Small-city patients pay for specialists, get 2 minutes
problem: Patients in smaller cities wait weeks for specialists, so they pay for online consults that get handed to a different doctor, downgraded to audio, cut to 2 minutes or cancelled without a refund. One instant consult cost roughly 3 times the doctor's own direct fee for a brief, poor consultation. They lose the fee and still leave with no diagnosis.
challenge: Make sure a patient who pays for a specialist gets that specialist, that time, or their money back.

title: The sender change that sank a course creator's emails
problem: Independent course creators keep their videos, students and mailing list with one host, so a single decision upstream can sink the business. In August 2026 a course host changed a creator's sender domain without notice and email open rates fell from about 30% to under 10%. Another Indian creator paid for a package whose promised website setup and marketing support never arrived.
challenge: Let an educator move their courses, students and emails anywhere in a day, and know the moment something breaks.

title: Freelancers chasing clients who stopped answering
problem: Freelancers face at least one unpaid invoice a month, burn hours drafting awkward follow-ups, and lose thousands to clients who vanish after receiving the final work. Reminders go out late or not at all, and invoicing, tracking and escalation are stitched across tools built for bigger companies.
challenge: Make sure a freelancer is paid before the final files leave their hands.

title: Warranty refused, so the same fault gets paid twice
problem: Local repair shops give no warranty on work or parts, and where one is promised it often is not honoured: in August 2026 an AC was still faulty after nearly ₹10,000 of repairs, and the warranty was refused. Pest control customers watch cockroaches or termites return within weeks or months, while warranty revisits are delayed or denied. Households end up paying again for the same fault.
challenge: Make a repair or pest control warranty something a household can claim in one message.

title: The tutor who can't say what last month earned
problem: Independent tutors enter payments by hand, cannot customise the invoices they send families, and track profit and loss outside the billing they already pay for. Splitting income with partner tutors happens on spreadsheets, and in August 2026 a long-time course creator called per-learner and transaction fees punishingly expensive as the business grew. UPI made fee collection instant, but matching it against fees and splits is still manual.
challenge: Show an independent tutor what each student and each month earned them, after every fee.

title: Crossed the GST threshold, and nobody showed you how
problem: Indian freelancers who cross the GST threshold must issue compliant invoices but rarely know how, while dues arrive as cash and bank transfers from many small clients that nobody reconciles. Very small firms find even the TDS return due every 3 months clumsy, so they pay for separate compliance software or an accountant. UPI turned dues into dozens of small transfers, and the rules keep tightening for earners who never had an accountant.
challenge: Make a freelancer's GST invoices, TDS records and who-has-paid list correct by default, without an accountant.

title: Kiranas losing their own street to quick commerce
problem: Neighbourhood kiranas and distributors say deep discounting by quick commerce is draining their footfall, and they have no way to compete on speed. Small food brands that try to join pay non-refundable listing fees per product and per state plus mandatory ad wallets, burning lakhs before seeing returns. Meanwhile shoppers who would happily order next-day from a local butcher or baker have no way to do it.
challenge: Let a neighbourhood food shop take next-day orders from its own street without paying to be listed.

title: Parcels stuck in the hub with nobody answering
problem: Parcels reach the destination city and then sit, or loop between hubs, for days or weeks with no updates and no office number that answers. In October 2026 a Delhivery parcel sat stuck for about 2 weeks while the recipient could not reach anyone, and a small seller shipping through Shiprocket lost clients when parcels went untraceable mid-route. No escalation path reaches a person who can find the box.
challenge: Find a stuck parcel and get it moving within 48 hours of it going quiet.

title: A blood test should not cost a day
problem: Rural patients travel tens of kilometres and lose a day for a basic test, and women in conservative areas delay tests over privacy and transport. Home packages booked online arrive missing tests, results are delayed, and refunds stall.
challenge: Get a basic blood test done and the report into the patient's hand within a day, wherever they live.

title: The course videos gone in one server crash
problem: In September 2026 an Indian course creator lost uploaded videos for good when the course host's server crashed, with no recovery offered. The same month, a long-time creator's membership account was terminated instantly, taking the content and the member list with it. Cloud services make it hard to download everything, so people find out they never had their own copy only after it is gone.
challenge: Keep a complete, usable copy of everything a creator has made and every fan they have, without them thinking about it.

title: The subscription that costs more every renewal
problem: Small firms find basic features locked behind premium add-ons, hidden costs after they buy, and a price rise every year with no way to push back. Usage-based AI pricing makes the monthly bill harder still to predict. One Indian buyer of Zoho Books hit hidden costs after purchase and got no useful answer from support for 7 months.
challenge: Cut a small company's subscription bill by a fifth without losing a feature it uses.

title: When the cook quits on Monday morning
problem: Families relying on a full-time domestic worker face chaos when she quits suddenly, with no stopgap help available. Parents who work late cannot find a verified, trustworthy babysitter for a few evening hours without hiring a full-time nanny, and prepaid household help can stay unavailable for months. Working parents lose workdays to gaps nobody can fill at short notice.
challenge: Find a family verified help for tonight or this week, without a month-long contract.

title: Hiring plans sold hard, then nobody answers
problem: Recruiters buy hiring plans after aggressive sales calls promising guarantees, then face early plan expiry, money-back promises that are never honoured, verification stuck for weeks and support that stays silent. Access to candidate databases costs more every quarter with no alternative of similar reach. Small employers end up paying again just to keep hiring.
challenge: Let a small employer see what each hiring channel delivered per rupee before renewing anything.

title: The work is done and the money never comes
problem: Money already earned arrives late or not at all: a freelancer sits through a 5-day security hold and then over a week of bank transfer, and contractors on international payroll services still go unpaid by foreign employers. One Indian startup shutdown left 300 staff jobless without notice, many unpaid for over a month. With no clear record of what is owed and no cheap way to press for it, most people swallow the loss.
challenge: Help someone owed money for finished work turn their records into a claim the payer cannot ignore.

title: The vendor who vanishes once the restaurant signs
problem: Restaurants sign up for billing and ordering systems, then support goes quiet, promised features never arrive, and one food business's Odoo rollout was still unfinished after a year. When the counter slows at peak hour or a vendor loses years of loyalty data, the restaurant pays in late orders and lost regulars. One Indian outlet on Petpooja said the vendor seemed busier signing new outlets than fixing its problems.
challenge: Get a small restaurant from one billing system to a better one in a weekend, with every record intact.

title: Job shops run production on spreadsheets and hope
problem: Generic ERPs cannot handle the routings, work orders and mixed production of a small job shop, so the shop falls back on spreadsheets. Customising an off-the-shelf system becomes a costly project, and even MaintainX cannot track one part held in several locations at different costs. Makers raised the same complaint in August 2025, March 2026 and April 2026.
challenge: Let a small job shop see every order's stage and material, set up in a week rather than a year.

title: Tiny ad budgets burned in a week
problem: Independent makers and small brands with tiny budgets find paid ads expensive and ineffective, and lack the time or skill to keep tuning low-budget campaigns. Money goes out every week with no clear sign of what worked.
challenge: Make ₹5,000 of ads teach a small seller something they can act on next week.

title: The day a PDF invoice stopped counting
problem: E-invoicing mandates reached smaller businesses in India and across Europe in 2025 and 2026, so a PDF sent by email no longer counts and small firms pay an intermediary to connect. One accounting service switched e-invoicing on without warning, and its clients missed invoices and waited on payments. A small Indian retailer found Zoho Books too rigid for retail GST rules and was left processing card payments by hand.
challenge: Get a small firm compliant with a new invoicing mandate in an afternoon, not a quarter.

title: Your property back home, and nobody watching it
problem: Indians living abroad fear encroachment on property left empty back home and get no real-time word from caretakers, a worry posted to Razorpay's Fix My Itch in January 2026. The managers they rely on fare little better: Buildium cannot handle more than one currency, and TenantCloud makes them pay for a higher plan to get owners' tax documents. So the owner never sees what the property earns or what is happening to it.
challenge: Give a property owner abroad a monthly statement and photo update they trust, in their own currency.

title: Paid for a resume, got a train ticket
problem: Small Indian employers pay a monthly fee to job portals and still get candidates living 30 km away for a job that needs someone within 2–3 km. One downloaded 50 resumes and found many were train tickets and blank pages, and another found a paid Naukri membership did not include contact details. Recruiters everywhere say mass-generated applications are burying the qualified people.
challenge: Get a neighbourhood employer 3 genuine, nearby candidates for an entry-level role within a week.

title: Outgrew the accounting package, cannot afford the ERP
problem: Small goods businesses outgrow entry-level accounting and inventory software, hitting order caps, drifting stock counts and integrations locked behind higher tiers. A traditional ERP costs too much and takes months, so they keep reconciling by hand.
challenge: Keep stock counts right across sales channels and books, without moving to an ERP.

title: The honest opinion that was a paid ad
problem: About 2 in 3 influencer ads that ASCI checked in India in 2025 failed disclosure rules, and some paid posts are deleted after the campaign so nobody can check later. Followers cannot tell an ad from an opinion. One fan who paid a scam creator profile on Patreon had the refund rejected without a person ever looking at it.
challenge: Let a follower check in seconds whether a creator's post was paid for and who paid.

title: The GST threshold you crossed without noticing
problem: Independent coaches and side-gig earners cross the GST threshold without knowing when registration kicks in, how to bill clients in the meantime or what they owe, and nobody tells them. Pulling together a profit and loss summary is tedious, so taxes get put off. The chartered accountant they see once a year comes in too late to plan anything.
challenge: Give a freelancer a running view of their tax position that is ready to hand to an accountant.

title: The customer who was never called back
problem: Small renovation and trade contractors cannot see which customers were contacted or still need an appointment, and Jobber gives them little reporting. Housecall Pro works on a phone but is a mess at the desk, and saves job-site photos only one at a time. As heat pump and solar upgrades grew in 2025, homeowners named unreliable contractors as the biggest thing holding them back.
challenge: Give a 2-person contractor a job book that keeps every customer, photo and follow-up straight from a phone.

title: Paying for profile boosts that nobody sees
problem: Job seekers pay for profile boosting and still see zero recruiter views for months, while their search visibility drops without explanation and sales calls push more upgrades. Many say they would rather pay for one guaranteed interview than keep paying to vanish into applicant pools.
challenge: Turn what a job seeker is willing to pay into a guaranteed conversation with a real hiring manager.

title: Next-day pay that lands a week late
problem: Small carriers cover fuel and payroll with factoring and quick pay, yet Truckstop's next-day quick pay waits 3–5 days on document checks and most factoring submissions land almost a week late. Factoring takes a large fee to reach money that is already owed. The cheap cash is never fast, and the fast cash is never cheap.
challenge: Get a small carrier paid within a day of delivery for less than a factoring fee.

title: Launched to a handful of likes, then silence
problem: Building software became nearly free by 2025, but solo founders launch to a handful of likes and have no repeatable way to reach buyers. Marketing feels alien, and most do not know where to begin. 3 years into the AI shift, Y Combinator notes that few new consumer products have reached ordinary people beyond chat assistants.
challenge: Get a solo founder's new product in front of 100 people who want it, within 2 weeks.

title: The WhatsApp invoice that arrives blank
problem: Small Indian shops find their billing crashes often, barcode printing fails and invoices shared on WhatsApp arrive as blank files, while Vyapar leaves their feature requests unanswered. Businesses with under 10 staff still work out salaries by hand each month, juggling leave, overtime and bonuses, because the payroll module in Tally needs training they cannot afford.
challenge: Make billing and monthly salaries for a 10-person shop take minutes and never fail at the counter.

title: Field crews derailed by an update nobody announced
problem: Small home-service contractors say Jobber and Housecall Pro lag when several jobs are open, push unannounced updates mid-job and schedule so weakly that the crew's day falls apart. In India, an independent RO repair professional is stuck as a third-party vendor on Urban Company, unable to get their own partner ID. The tradesperson does the work while somebody else's system decides how the day goes.
challenge: Let a solo tradesperson run their own bookings and schedule without depending on an aggregator's system.

title: Payroll errors found only after salaries go out
problem: Small firms pay for all-in-one HR suites that feel expensive for their size and still get payroll data errors, missing tax forms and income tax computed wrong for a whole year. Support lacks product knowledge or takes a week, so mistakes surface after salaries go out and HR fixes them by hand.
challenge: Catch every payroll and tax mistake before salaries go out, not after employees complain.

title: The truck never came and nobody knows why
problem: Small manufacturers book local transporters who never turn up, leaving finished goods stuck at the factory and delivery deadlines missed. Regional transporters give no live tracking, so customers keep calling for updates. A container's pickup number passes through 4 hands before it reaches the driver, owner to forwarder to broker to trucker, and every delay runs up storage fees.
challenge: Give a small factory and its buyer a live view of every regional truck booking, from pickup to delivery.

title: Reach that drops to zero with no explanation
problem: Short videos that used to reach tens of thousands now sit at zero, second posts in a day get a fraction of the first, and accepting a collaboration post can cut reach sharply. Creators cannot tell which choice caused the drop, so they change everything at once and learn nothing.
challenge: Show a creator which of their own choices moved reach this week, using only their own numbers.

title: Cryptic UPI names turn every statement into a puzzle
problem: Spending is scattered across UPI, cards, wallets and subscriptions, and cryptic merchant names make small payments impossible to recall weeks later. Budgeting that needs manual entry gets abandoned within weeks, and bank sync shows up late or not at all.
challenge: Tell someone where their money went last month without asking them to type anything.

title: Shift rosters and hourly attendance kept on paper
problem: HR software is built for salaried desk staff, so shift workers cannot fix a forgotten clock-in, managers cannot see who is off on a given day, and recurring rosters must be recopied every few months. Hours from swipe cards and deskless staff do not export cleanly into payroll, and volunteers do not fit at all, so every pay run starts with manual fixes.
challenge: Make the weekly roster and the hours that reach payroll match without anybody retyping them.

title: Phone editors that eat a creator's work
problem: Short-video editors on phones lose drafts when redo fails, drop edits when several overlays stack and freeze on export. The saved file sometimes does not even match the edit, so hours of work vanish right before posting.
challenge: Make sure no creator ever loses a finished edit, whatever happens to the editor on their phone.

title: The changelog nobody read until payroll broke
problem: Software makers ship breaking changes with little warning, and customers either miss the changelog or never get one, so the first notice is an outage. In August 2025, a people team at a real estate firm on greytHR found features changed without notice and payroll calculated wrong, with no support contact to call. Teams that do write release notes rewrite them several times, for engineers and for non-technical readers.
challenge: Make sure every customer learns about a change that affects them, in their own terms, before it ships.

title: Share your own work and get banned as spam
problem: Independent makers who share their own work in online communities get flagged as spammers unless they are long-standing members, and Substack's spam filters have blocked a writer from linking to their own site. After generated posts flooded communities in 2025, moderators tightened self-promotion rules just as more people began shipping. The people with the most reason to talk about their work are the ones the rules silence.
challenge: Help an independent maker earn a community's trust fast enough to share their work there within a month.

title: Half the workday spent saying what you did
problem: Employees spend hours in status meetings that a short written update could replace, yet engineers will not keep task boards current after stand-ups. Managers get guesswork, and the people doing the work are interrupted again and again to feed status reports.
challenge: Give managers an accurate status of every task without one meeting or one manual board update.

title: Scheduled posts that quietly never go out
problem: Small businesses pay Buffer and Later to schedule social posts, then watch tags drop, the Instagram connection fail and posts never publish. One was charged a large annual fee right after the trial and refused a refund despite cancelling the same day, and another, double-charged, could reach only AI bots and never a person. Owners who do not use social media themselves get no traction at all as organic reach shrinks.
challenge: Give a small business a month of posts that go out on time, every time, with proof that they did.

title: A dozen tabs checked before the day begins
problem: Founders of small teams spend half an hour every morning checking a dozen services for code changes, messages and payments, and constant switching between tabs, chats and email breaks deep focus. Small teams can now build big companies on little capital, but the means to run that lean are still immature. With a handful of people doing what once took dozens, all that watching falls on 1 or 2 of them.
challenge: Give a small-team founder one morning briefing that replaces checking a dozen services.

title: Lakhs of followers, and the sales never came
problem: A Mumbai skincare founder paid a creator with lakhs of followers for 4 Reels; the reach looked fine, but sales never followed. Indian D2C brands have dropped agencies to deal with creators directly, so the vetting falls on founders, and nearly 3 in 4 brands call fake followers a major challenge. First-time founders on small budgets cannot even tell whether a campaign worked.
challenge: Tell a small brand, before it pays, whether a creator's audience is real and likely to buy.

title: The shop website nobody has ever checked
problem: Small firms running websites and online stores cannot afford accessibility audits or security checks, so people on screen readers are shut out and malware or holes go unnoticed. Since 2025, shopping and booking agents have browsed the web on people's behalf, yet sites are still built for humans clicking buttons. A store an agent cannot use is now a store losing sales.
challenge: Tell a small online store, in one afternoon, what stops a blind shopper, an attacker or a buying agent on its site.

title: A calm media diet nobody curates
problem: People hunt for focus music through ads and endless playlists, struggle to stay informed without the stress of the news cycle, and lack an easy way to listen to saved articles. Book recommendations rarely match their taste, and cheap generative media has not yet become something they use every day.
challenge: Give someone a daily mix of reading, news and listening that fits their taste and leaves them calmer, not more anxious.

title: Job ad budgets burned on clicks, not hires
problem: Small employers find free job posts get no visibility, sponsored posts and pay-per-click ads always spend the full monthly budget, and job board subscriptions can quadruple in price while results get worse. What arrives is a flood of irrelevant, mass-produced applications, so the cost per real hire keeps rising for businesses that can least afford it.
challenge: Cut a small employer's cost per genuine applicant in half without raising their job ad spend.

title: The job offer that asks for a laptop deposit
problem: Job seekers on WorkIndia have found fake tech postings demanding a laptop deposit, and fake take-home coding tests plant malware or harvest unpaid work. Employers on the same site get candidates who lie about availability and leads that turn out fake, with no support once they have paid. Complaints from January 2025, May 2026 and July 2026 tell the same story: neither side can trust a first contact.
challenge: Let a job seeker check, in under a minute, whether a job offer or test is real before they pay or download anything.

title: Job matches that ignore everything you said
problem: Job seekers on Naukri report that almost every recommended job is unrelated to their profile, and posting a profile brings a flood of spam calls and messages. Listings marked remote often turn out to be restricted by region, so hours go into filtering roles that were never a real fit.
challenge: Cut the jobs a seeker has to read by 90%, while missing none that truly fit.

title: Every AI conversation starts from zero
problem: People who lean on AI assistants lose old conversations once dozens pile up in a day, keep reusable prompts scattered across notes, and repeat the same background to every assistant they use. Assistants added memory and project spaces in 2025, but each keeps its own. Those chats are private by design, so a team cannot build on each other's work with agents the way it does in a shared document.
challenge: Make what a person or team has already told any AI assistant findable and reusable everywhere they work.

title: A year of building, and not one paying customer
problem: Solo builders spend a year on a working product beside a day job, then stall at a few dozen people, because distribution, not engineering, is the bottleneck. Cold emails to small firms go unanswered in inboxes flooded by generated outreach, and demo videos go unwatched. Individuals rarely pay for small web products themselves, even when their employers would pay for one that saves the team time.
challenge: Get a solo builder's working product its first 10 paying customers in 3 weeks.

title: Code ships faster than anyone can check it
problem: Coding agents multiplied how much code a small team ships in 2025, but startups without testers cannot keep quality up, and tiny companies grep raw logs instead of getting an alert when production breaks. Developers test build pipelines through commit after commit because they cannot reproduce that environment locally. Too often, the first person to find the bug is a customer.
challenge: Catch the bug a small team's AI-written code introduced before a customer does, without hiring a tester.
